newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks shake off early weakness, set record.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks shake off early weakness, set record.

text.p: Swiss shares shook off early weakness to end at a record closing high on Monday, propelled by a firming dollar which drove up stocks of export-dependent companies, dealers said.
Early gains on Wall Street and derivatives-linked transactions also helped the rise.
"We have seen extreme moves in some shares, which points to a lot of action in derivatives," one trader noted.
"As long as the environment stays like this, people will keep buying," he added.
Activity was described as lively. Volume hit 2.26 billion Swiss francs.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 37.9 points, or 0.76 percent, at 5,042.6. The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 19.57 points, or 0.62 percent, to 3,187.56.
Index heavyweights such as Novartis, Roche and Nestle, which had dragged the indices down in early trade, changed course at midday, leading the recovery of the whole market, one dealer added.
Novartis registereds edged up three francs to 1,983. Roche were up 50 francs at 12,730 after a low of 12,585.
Among banks, UBS bearer shares climbed five francs to 1,405. SBC firmed 5.50 francs to 346.50. Credit Suisse jumped 3.75 francs to 173.0.
Shares of insurer Winterthur were sought ahead of 1996 results which are expected on Wednesday after trading closes, one dealer noted.
Ciba Specialty Chemicals powered ahead 3.75 francs to 135.25, partially due to derivatives transactions.

ABB, Surveillance and Baloise also saw gains of more than two percent. Inspection firm Surveillance said a Swiss tax panel had confirmed SGS's position in a dispute over the tax treatment of share buybacks.
